correctness.rationale: From the published exact stationary weight, at N=M the K-particle backbone weights have exact ratio R_k=(L-k)/(k+1)q^{-(k+1)}(1-q^{-(M-k)})/(1-q^{-(k+1)}). Consecutive ratios decrease by at least q^{-1}, proving uniform discrete-Gaussian tails about a mode. The mode solves (log q)m+log m=log L+O(1). Conditional uniform ring placements give J=(h_f-h_b)E[K(L-K)]/[L(L-1)], yielding the stated log and loglog asymptotic; configuration complementation proves the reciprocal parameter identity. Standalone verification passed 86 deterministic assertions including finite CTMC generator checks; finite tests are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact capacity matching N=M separates branch filling from extensive backbone transport in the source model. The stationary current decays as log L/L rather than the naive finite-defect 1/L and has a universal negative loglog correction; this quantifies the otherwise visually almost blocked regime. Uniform O(1) occupancy fluctuations distinguish critical finite-size leakage from an extensive particle reservoir. Reciprocal-bias duality transfers the prediction to the opposite critical filling. These are structural, interpretable predictions for particle transport along finite network dead ends, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
